claims.text: With no backend set, OpenTofu writes the state after apply to its default file terraform.tfstate in the configuration's folder, plain-text JSON when no encryption is set (as in first-cluster); it maps each resource address to the remote object and attributes read back.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State (purpose: mapping to real world, metadata); Language > Settings > Backends > local (default path terraform.tfstate)

claims.text: A resource address for a resource in the root configuration is <type>.<local name>, such as kind_cluster.this; plans and tofu state list use it.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > State > Resource Addressing; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt lines 1-2

claims.text: A value is marked sensitive with sensitive = true (e.g. in a variable block); OpenTofu hides such values in plan and apply output, printing (sensitive value) instead; sensitive values are still recorded in the state.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State > Sensitive Data; Language > Values > Variables (sensitive) / Outputs (sensitive)

claims.text: By default tofu plan reads the current values of the objects recorded in the state, then compares with the configuration; an address only in the configuration is planned for creation; one only in the state, with nothing about it in the configuration (no removed block), for destruction.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > Commands > tofu plan (reads current state of existing objects; proposes create/destroy); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt lines 7-14

claims.text: Removing the resource block while kind_cluster.this is in the state makes the plan print '# kind_cluster.this will be destroyed' and '# (because kind_cluster.this is not in configuration)', 'Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.'; apply would then delete the object.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt lines 7-10 (real run); opentofu.org docs: Language > Resources > Behavior (destroy resources no longer in configuration)

claims.text: kubectl apply -f without --prune sends only the objects in the given manifests and does not delete an object whose manifest was removed; Đơn Hàng's scripts never pass --prune.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io docs: Tasks > Manage Kubernetes Objects > Declarative Management (How to delete objects; --prune alternative); grep --prune in examples/don-hang/scripts: no match

claims.text: OpenTofu does not look up existing remote objects by name or attributes: with no state, every resource in the configuration is planned for creation ('kind_cluster.this will be created', 'Plan: 1 to add').
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State (Purpose: mapping configuration to the real world; importing is the way to adopt existing objects); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt lines 12-14

claims.text: Creating a kind cluster whose name an existing cluster already uses fails; through tehcyx/kind 0.11.0 the apply prints 'Error: node(s) already exist for a cluster with the name "donhang-iac"'.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt line 15 (real run); kind source pkg/cluster/internal/create (node(s) already exist for a cluster with the name)

claims.text: tofu apply with a saved plan file refuses it when the state changed after the plan was created, printing 'Error: Saved plan is stale' and exiting non-zero (exit 1 here).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt lines 17-24 (real run, OpenTofu 1.10.10); opentofu.org docs: CLI > Commands > tofu apply (Saved Plan Mode)

claims.text: tofu apply -auto-approve skips the interactive 'yes' approval before applying.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > Commands > tofu apply (-auto-approve)

claims.text: tofu state list prints the resource addresses recorded in the state, one per line (here only kind_cluster.this).
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > Commands > state list; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt lines 1-2

claims.text: The state of first-cluster holds the kind_cluster attribute client_key in plain text: the private key of the client credential in the cluster's kubeconfig, the one kubectl uses to reach donhang-iac.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-state.txt lines 4-5; search.opentofu.org tehcyx/kind 0.11.0 kind_cluster (client_key); kind docs: Quick Start (kubeconfig, admin user)

claims.text: tofu-state.sh runs in deploy/tofu/lessons/first-cluster after tofu-plan-apply.sh; it prints only the first line of client_key, removes main.tf from the plan-and-apply comment onward with perl, moves the state away and back, and restores every file with mv and trap.
Đơn Hàng's .gitignore at stage-3 ignores *.tfstate (line 27) and *.tfstate.*, with a comment that state files hold credentials in plain text.
git check-ignore -v <path> prints the matching source, line number and pattern followed by the path, in the form '.gitignore:27:*.tfstate<TAB>deploy/tofu/lessons/first-cluster/terraform.tfstate'.
When you mean to keep an object whose block you remove, read the plan for 'will be destroyed' before typing yes.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu apply (review the plan before approving)

claims.text: The state must not be committed to Git when it holds credentials in plain text, because anyone who can read the repository could use them.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State > Sensitive Data (treat state as sensitive); devops.l1.secrets-vs-config
